notes: Cliffside Park holds QUAM (Qualified Urban Aid Municipality) status under the Fourth Round, making it exempt from the standard prospective-need new-construction obligation. A dedicated Fourth Round Housing Element and Fair Share Plan page exists on the municipal website. No library.njcourts.gov HEFSP document was found for Cliffside Park specifically, suggesting the borough may be proceeding under QUAM provisions rather than filing a full HEFSP with the Affordable Housing Dispute Resolution Program. Specific present-need and prospective-need unit counts were not surfaced by search results; numeric obligations are likely zero or near-zero due to QUAM status. No development sites were identified in search results.

notes: Closter's Fourth Round obligation is 241 affordable units. The borough has a zero-unit RDP (vacant land adjustment), yielding 241 units of unmet need. The law requires providing realistic zoning for at least 25% of unmet need (61 units). HEFSP adopted June 26, 2025 by Planning Board and endorsed same day by Borough Council. Mechanisms include an Affordable Housing Overlay (AHO) District over Commercial (District 4) and Industrial (District 5 and 5A) areas at 12 units/acre density with 20% set-aside; owner-occupied townhouses permitted at 8 units/acre with 20% set-aside. Village School Commons (511 Durie Ave) is a fully separate 100%-affordable 35-unit project (groundbreaking January 21, 2026) financed with 4% LIHTC and bond financing. Ordinance 2025-1352 provided $2M grant to the Village School developer. Specific individual site block/lot numbers beyond Village School not surfaced in searches.

notes: Cresskill has a Fourth Round prospective need of 155 units and zero present need (rehabilitation). The borough's RDP was found to be zero after vacant land assessment, making all 155 units unmet need. Borough must provide realistic zoning for at least 25% (approximately 39 units). A fully executed settlement agreement with FSHC exists. HEFSP is endorsed and signed, filed with library.njcourts.gov. Borough continues Third-Round overlay programs and modifies them for Fourth Round, specifically increasing density and set-aside on Block 181, Lot 1. Existing mandatory set-aside applies to developments of 5+ market-rate units. Set-aside is 15% for rental, 20% for for-sale. Specific settlement date not identified in search results.

notes: Demarest's Joint Planning Board adopted the 2025 Housing Element & Fair Share Plan (prepared by Colliers Engineering & Design, dated May 16, 2025) on June 5, 2025, via Resolution RES-JPB-009-25. Borough Council endorsed it and it was filed with the Affordable Housing Dispute Resolution Program. The plan implements multiple mechanisms: (1) Accessory Apartment Program administered by Housing Authority of Bergen County - subsidy of $25,000/low-income unit and $20,000/moderate-income unit (max creditable = 10 or 10% of obligation, whichever is greater); (2) Downtown Rehabilitation/Redevelopment Area centered on Hardenburgh Avenue (11.2 acres, 23 tax lots including Block 23 Lots 9-23 and Blocks 46 and 49.01) - Ordinance 1177-26 (March 12, 2026) adopted amended Redevelopment Plan by Colliers Engineering to conform to 2025 HEFSP; (3) Overlay zones for unmet need. Implementing ordinances: Ord. 1173-26 (accessory apt subsidies), Ord. 1174-26, Ord. 1175-26 (development fees), Ord. 1176-26 (affordable housing regulations, replacing Article X), Ord. 1177-26 (amended redevelopment plan). HEFSP was amended and a public hearing held February 4, 2026. Specific total obligation unit counts (present need/prospective need) not confirmed in search results; the HEFSP document at library.njcourts.gov should contain those figures.

notes: Dumont's adopted Fourth Round HEFSP (Exhibit B) was filed with library.njcourts.gov on June 11, 2025. Dumont is a dense, mature municipality designated Metropolitan Planning Area (PA1) with effectively zero RDP from vacant land. The borough previously received a Judgment of Compliance and Repose on March 8, 2019 covering through July 1, 2025. The Fourth Round plan relies heavily on redevelopment-area infill sites. Two specific sites identified: (1) The Crescent - a redevelopment project expected to generate 48 total units with 7 affordable (15% set-aside rental), with an additional 3.5 infill bonus credits for 10.5 total credits; (2) 125 Washington Avenue (Block 1216, Lot 1) - multi-family rental above existing retail, 1 affordable unit with 0.5 infill bonus for 1.5 total credits. Note: information about these sites from search result synthesis may partially reflect the Third Round/amended plan context; the Fourth Round HEFSP document at njcourts.gov should be verified directly for current unit counts. Specific total Fourth Round obligation units (present need and prospective need) not surfaced by search results.
